title: Discrepancy integrand as a signed indicator difference
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be arbitrary types, let $g : X \times Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$ (written $g(x,y)$), let $S \subseteq X \times Y$, and let $\sigma : \mathrm{Bool} \to \bbr$ send $\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and $\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$. Then for every point $(x,y) \in X \times Y$,
\[
\mathbf{1}_{S}(x,y)\,\sigma\bigl(g(x,y)\bigr)
= \mathbf{1}_{\{(x,y)\in S \,:\, g(x,y)=\mathrm{false}\}}(x,y)
- \mathbf{1}_{\{(x,y)\in S \,:\, g(x,y)=\mathrm{true}\}}(x,y),
\]
where each indicator takes the value $1$ on its set and $0$ elsewhere.
hypotheses_covered: a fixed point (x,y) in X × Y
σ = boolSign sending false to 1 and true to −1
replaced:
For any $g : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$, $S \subseteq X \times Y$, and point
$(x,y) \in X \times Y$, the pointwise integrand
$\mathbf{1}_{S}(x,y)\cdot\sigma(g(x,y))$
equals the indicator of $\{(x,y)\in S \mid g(x,y)=\mathrm{false}\}$ minus the
indicator of $\{(x,y)\in S \mid g(x,y)=\mathrm{true}\}$ evaluated at $(x,y)$.
